content_html:
Visiting Machu Picchu by train is one of the most comfortable and panoramic ways to reach the Inca citadel. There are different train and route options, so it is important to plan your trip well. Here we tell you everything you need to know to live an unforgettable experience.

Train options to get to Machu Picchu

Currently, there are two companies that operate the train service to Machu Picchu:

1. PeruRail

It is the most traditional option, with different service categories:

  • Expedition: The most economical option, with comfortable seats and panoramic windows.
  • Vistadome: With larger windows and glass roof to enjoy the Andean landscape.
  • Hiram Bingham: A luxury train with gourmet food and live music, ideal for those looking for a premium experience.

2. Inca Rail

It offers a similar experience with different categories:

  • Voyager: The standard, economical and comfortable option.
  • The 360°: With larger windows to enjoy the landscape.
  • The First Class: A premium service with lunch on board.
  • The Private: An exclusive experience in a private luxury carriage.

Where to take the train from?

There are three main stations to board the train to Machu Picchu:

1. Cusco (Poroy)

Location: 30 minutes from the center of Cusco.
Advantage: It is ideal if you want to leave directly from Cusco.
Disadvantage: It only operates in the dry season (April to December).

2. Ollantaytambo

Location: In the Sacred Valley, 1 hour and 45 minutes from Cusco.
Advantage: Greater frequency of trains and spectacular landscapes.
Disadvantage: You have to travel first from Cusco to Ollantaytambo.

3. San Pedro (Cusco) – New option

Location: Historic center of Cusco.
Advantage: More comfortable alternative to board the train without leaving Cusco.
Disadvantage: It has fewer daily departures.

Tips for buying train tickets

  • Book in advance: Especially in high season (June-August), as tickets sell out quickly.
  • Compare prices: Both companies offer promotions on their websites.
  • Choose the right time: The morning trains allow you to make the most of the day at Machu Picchu, while the afternoon trains offer a calmer experience.

Practical tips for traveling by train

Carry a small backpack: Only hand luggage is allowed on trains (maximum 5 kg).
Wear comfortable, layered clothing: The weather can vary between hot and cold along the way.
Don't forget your passport or ID: It is mandatory to enter the train and Machu Picchu.
Take advantage of the trip to enjoy the landscape: During the journey you will see mountains, rivers and archaeological remains.

Last stretch: From Aguas Calientes to Machu Picchu

Once in Aguas Calientes, you can climb Machu Picchu in two ways:
Bus (25 min, $12 approx.) – The most comfortable option.
Walking (1h 30 min approx.) – For the most adventurous and in good physical condition.
